definition: Nibbāna understood as present or immediate in this very life.
notes: Keep the rendering tied to early-text liberation usage and avoid overloading the term with later metaphysical systematization. The phrase belongs in the nibbāna family and should not be rewritten into generic worldly happiness or premature-finality language.

example_phrases.translation: they describe supreme here-and-now nibbāna on five grounds
example_phrases.notes: The five here-and-now-nibbāna doctrines in DN 1. The record previously cited MN 13, the Mahādukkhakkhandha Sutta, which contains no form of `nibbāna` at all; the strict verifier returned `inconclusive` because MN 13 uses peyyāla. DN 1 is not a translated surface, so the record stays orphaned. Repaired in the 2026-09-13 Wave 11 audit.
